physical_skill: Recover actual blade rotation by gripping and extracting a loose offcut through an original-scale wire guard, then release it into a tray and verify ten seconds of forward operation. Source CAD preserves frame, rotor, wire guard and controller surroundings. The impeller is initially stalled by mesh contact, not a scoring state or attachment.
valid_shortcuts: A direct external guarded pull without switching off is valid when fingers and tools stay outside the rotor access boundary; the demonstrated route uses this.
Switching off and waiting for rest before internal service is valid; manual motion after rest does not count as motor coasting.
Either hand and either supplied tool may be used if the physical contact, release and safety conditions hold.

Holding the strip in the tray earns clearance only, not containment/full credit. Reverse rotation does not establish cooling operation. Fixed fasteners cannot be removed in this task; the model does not simulate fracture.
distinct_from_nearest: Accepted #1441 severs a tightened cable tie with cutters around a supported cable bundle and checks insulation damage; this task extracts an already loose offcut from real rotating hardware and verifies recovered operation, with no cutting mechanism. Closed #2188 is fan installation by snap-fit and lacks chassis/wires; this uses actual controller, heatsink, guard and wired fan contacts, with no insertion latch. Revising #2189 reassembles a household fan with keyed shaft and clips; this retains the assembly and clears a physical jam. Revising #2055 installs a server shroud; no shroud/tab seating is involved here. Rejected #404 swaps fan modules; neither fan replacement nor hot-swap sequence is required. Pending #1273 unfolds a hand fan, an unrelated mechanism. Live comments for #1441/#2188/#2189/#2055 were reread before this review. Our concurrent dishwasher candidate shares the broad recovery theme, but its defining manipulation is a full-size 300 mm spatula through a free wheeled rack and appliance opening, with basket retention/return and a low-torque full-turn clearance test. This fan task has a fixed 40 mm rotor assembly, a 3 x 1 mm offcut extracted through a 4.25 mm wire-guard gap, powered/coasting rotor-access constraints, and sustained 4000 RPM motor recovery. The contact clearances, movable assembly constraints and operational validation differ beyond object identity or category.
risks: Rigid offcut omits bending and fracture; limits are explicit, and no fracture-detection claim is made.
Conservative tool collision bounds intentionally reject powered access at the blade envelope; actual damaging tool entry was not demonstrated by free-drop diagnostics.
This is a source-scale open development controller on documented standoffs, not a claimed server or enclosed robot service chassis.
